title: OIDC Front-Channel Logout
subtitle: The IdP loads one hidden iframe per app so each clears its own session — fully browser-visible, but best-effort and easily partial on modern browsers.

steps.label: Logout already initiated
steps.lede: A logout has begun — typically RP-Initiated Logout reached the IdP’s end_session_endpoint. The IdP now needs to propagate it to every app in the SSO session.
steps.devtools: Open DevTools (F12) → Network, enable Preserve log (the logout page navigates away). Unlike back-channel logout, every step here is browser-visible — that is the whole point of the front channel.

steps.label: Logout page with hidden iframes
steps.lede: The IdP terminates the SSO session and returns an HTML page containing one hidden <iframe> per RP that joined it — each pointing at that RP’s frontchannel_logout_uri.

headers: idp_session=; Path=/; Max-Age=0; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=None

steps.devtools: Filter on end_session. Open the Response tab and read the HTML — its body lists one hidden <iframe> per RP. Those src URLs are what the browser fetches next.

steps.label: RP1 iframe fires — cookie present
steps.lede: The browser loads RP1’s logout iframe. Its own session cookie rides along, so RP1 can validate iss/sid and clear the session — a clean logout.

headers: rp1_session=; Path=/; Max-Age=0; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax

steps.devtools: Filter on frontchannel-logout. Check the Request Cookies — rp1_session was sent — and the Response Set-Cookie clears it (Max-Age=0). Cookie sent + cookie cleared = that RP is logged out. The sid query param must match the sid claim from that RP’s ID token.

steps.label: RP2 iframe fires — cookie blocked
steps.lede: RP2’s iframe loads too, but as a third-party frame the browser partitions/blocks its cookie. With no session cookie visible, RP2 has nothing to clear — a partial logout.
steps.devtools: Same filter. Here the Request Cookies are empty — rp2_session was partitioned/dropped — and there is no Set-Cookie in the response. The frame returned 200 but nothing was cleared: partial logout, and RP2’s session survives. This is the expected outcome on current browsers.

steps.label: Return to post_logout_redirect_uri
steps.lede: After a fixed timeout the IdP proceeds to the RP’s post_logout_redirect_uri. This return leg fires regardless of whether the frames succeeded — there is no acknowledgement channel.
steps.devtools: Filter on loggedout. A 200 here does not confirm every RP was logged out — front-channel logout is best-effort. Also watch the Console: an RP that sends X-Frame-Options: DENY or a restrictive frame-ancestors CSP produces a “Refused to display in a frame” error, and the IdP gets no signal either way.

steps.label: “Logged out everywhere” (best effort)
steps.lede: The user sees a logged-out confirmation. But as the RP2 frame showed, that message is optimistic — a partitioned cookie means at least one app’s session may still be alive.
steps.devtools: Conclusion from the capture: frame 200 + cookie sent + cookie cleared → logged out; frame 200 + cookie missing → partial logout. Where reliability matters, pair or replace this with back-channel logout, whose server-to-server delivery does not depend on third-party cookies.
